entry.title: Tesla turns to Turo to boost adoption of Full Self-Driving (Supervised)
entry.summary: Eligible Turo hosts will also get a one-month free trial of Tesla's FSD software.

entry.title: Matiks raises $10M to expand its math and puzzle gaming platform
entry.summary: Matiks has introduced a new platform for users to create games using AI.

entry.title: Apple unveils new iPad mini with OLED display and faster A20 Pro chip
entry.summary: The new iPad mini features a thinner and lighter design than its predecessor.

entry.title: Anthropic officially files for its public debut
entry.summary: Anthropic has officially filed for an IPO, revealing soaring revenue, mounting losses, major enterprise adoption, and an unusual governance structure designed to preserve founder control and its AI safety mission.

entry.title: Microsoft offers buyouts to around 60,000 employees
entry.summary: The buyout offers mark Microsoft's latest efforts to cut costs and rework its workforce.

entry.title: SpaceX locks in $40B GPU financing deal with Apollo
entry.summary: The financing gives SpaceX another way to fund its rapidly expanding AI ambitions without relying solely on traditional debt markets.

entry.title: Anthropic’s IPO filing reveals its strategy for keeping enterprise customers hooked
entry.summary: Anthropic’s S-1 shows more than half of its $100,000-plus customers now use both the Claude Platform and a first-party app, a cross-selling playbook reminiscent of Amazon that’s making enterprise customers stickier.

entry.title: This startup’s self-driving excavators help dig up $600M in new funding
entry.summary: Bedrock Robotics, which is now valued at $4.1 billion, is particularly focused on autonomous excavators, in part because of a growing shortage of skilled operators.

entry.title: Fusion startups are giving the government shares in exchange for awards. Is it worth it?
entry.summary: Fusion startups face a new challenge, one unrelated to plasma physics: Give the government shares in exchange for funding awards or go it alone?

entry.title: Uh-oh, it sounds like the iPhone Duo keeps cracking and users aren’t happy about it
entry.summary: A small number of early adopters of the much-hyped new foldable phone from Apple have complained of screens cracking.

entry.title: Watch out, YouTube — Instagram goes from short-form to 90-minute videos
entry.summary: After years in which every social platform (even LinkedIn!) aggressively pursued short-form video, this is a notable shift in strategy for Instagram.

entry.title: Databricks co-founder shares his secrets for winning big enterprise customers
entry.summary: Turns out selling to big companies isn’t about having the shiniest tech: It’s about hitching a ride on a giant’s sales team.

entry.title: Cohere says Alibaba’s Qwen model tried to send a file to Beijing
entry.summary: An AI model said it wouldn’t use any tools, then tried to send something to a server in Beijing anyway, and while researchers say it’s probably a training quirk and not espionage, the whole thing has people asking how much to trust free Chinese AI.

entry.title: How OpenAI turned its coding tools into dots, an always-on personal assistant
entry.summary: Alexander Embiricos, the OpenAI executive responsible for dots, never wants to have a meeting with someone else's AI agent.

entry.title: X is nudging users to promote their posts with a pointing hand, and people are confused
entry.summary: Whose hand is behind this travesty?

entry.title: Nvidia backs Indian startup helping companies run AI models with fewer GPUs
entry.summary: Simplismart says its annualized revenue run rate has grown 14-fold in six months, with the U.S. accounting for more than half its revenue.

entry.title: Opera introduces a new web standard to let users deploy AI locally in their browser
entry.summary: The new standard, WebAI, is designed to work with a variety of AI models.

entry.title: General Compute raises $100 million Series A, countering the neocloud disaster narrative
entry.summary: General Compute is betting on inference chips from outside the Nvidia ecosystem.

entry.title: Anduril, Qualcomm launch BlueChip, a new kind of US-made laptop
entry.summary: Anduril founder Palmer Luckey is vowing to bring computer manufacturing back to the U.S. and by that he doesn't just mean assembly, but every individual component, some of which are exclusively made in China today.

entry.title: Billionaire Palmer Luckey isn’t leaving California over the wealth tax
entry.summary: "It's causing a lot of people to run who I don't want to be running," native Californian Palmer Luckey said. "But I'm planning on staying in California. I'm going to keep fighting it."
